'''Frank P. Ryan''' (born 1944) is a British consultant physician, [[evolutionary biologist]] and historian of science. He is a pioneer of viral [[symbiosis]] in the evolution of the human genome.

==Biography==

Ryan was born in [[Limerick]] and moved to England at the age of 12.<ref name="Biography">[https://swiftpublishers.com/welcome-to-swift-publishers/frank-ryan-biography/ "Biography"]. swiftpublishers.com. Retrieved 5 February 2023.</ref> He was educated at [[Thornleigh Salesian College]] and the [[Bolton Institute of Technology]]. He qualified MD from [[Sheffield Medical School]] in 1970.<ref name="Biography"/><ref name="thirdway">[https://www.thethirdwayofevolution.com/people/view/frank-p.-ryan "Frank P. Ryan"]. thethirdwayofevolution.com. Retrieved 5 February 2023.</ref> Ryan is a Medical Adviser to Sheffield Primary Care Trust and an Honorary Research Fellow in Evolutionary Biology at the Department of Animal and Plant Sciences, [[Sheffield University]].<ref name="fabresearch">[https://www.fabresearch.org/viewItem.php?id=7415 Dr Frank Ryan]. fabresearch.org. Retrieved 5 February 2023.</ref> He is a Fellow of the [[Linnean Society of London]], [[Royal Society of Medicine]] and the [[Royal College of Physicians]].<ref name="fabresearch"/><ref>[https://www.harpercollins.com.au/cr-102188/frank-ryan/ Frank Ryan]. harpercollins.com.au. Retrieved 5 February 2023.</ref>

==Research==

Ryan has introduced concepts such as aggressive symbiosis, viral symbiosis and holobiontic genome to evolutionary biology which have been developed by other colleagues.<ref name="thirdway"/><ref>[https://jonathanpegg.com/clients-books/frank-ryan/ "Dr Frank Ryan"]. jonathanpegg.com. Retrieved 5 February 2023.</ref>

In 1990, Ryan co-authored ''The Eskimo Diet'' with Reg Saynor. The book modern revealed the importance of [[omega-3 fatty acid]]s in the diet and argued that consumption of fish oils can reduce the risk of heart disease.<ref>{{cite journal|year=1990|title=The Eskimo Diet: How to Avoid a Heart Attack|journal=Polar Record|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/polar-record/article/eskimo-diet-how-to-avoid-a-heart-attack-r-saynor-and-f-ryan-1990-london-ebury-press-192-p-illustrated-soft-cover-isbn-0852238096-599/9D292FCE67258219AE3ADBB3274A78FB|volume=26|issue=159|pages=339|doi=10.1017/S0032247400012092|doi-access=free}}</ref> The same year, he co-authored ''The Eskimo Diet Cookbook''.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20211002082825/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/the-war-on-blubber-n9h0xzqd9lm|title="The war on blubber"}}. thetimes.co.uk. Retrieved 5 February 2023.</ref>

Ryan's book ''Darwin's Blind Spot: Evolution Beyond Natural Selection'', published in 2002 argued that [[Charles Darwin]] had an incomplete view of evolution as he missed the role of symbiosis in the evolution of life. The book has been positively reviewed in academic journals.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Klein, J. C. von Vaupel|year=2003|title=Reviewed Work: Darwin's Blind Spot by F. Ryan|journal=Crustaceana|volume=76|issue=2|pages=255|jstor=20105560}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Cech, Paul J.|year=2004|title=Darwin's Blind Spot: Evolution Beyond Natural Selection|journal=The Quarterly Review of Biology|url=https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/10.1086/425772|volume=79|issue=3|pages=304|doi=10.1086/425772|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Ryan's ''Metamorphosis'', published in 2011 describes the pioneering contributions of [[Vincent Wigglesworth]] and [[Carroll Williams]] to insect metamorphosis and more controversially the research of [[Donald I. Williamson]] who believed that metamorphosis is the result of the hybridization of distinct life forms.<ref>[https://newint.org/columns/media/books/2011/07/01/metamorphosis-frank-ryan "Book Review: Metamorphosis"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230206001757/https://newint.org/columns/media/books/2011/07/01/metamorphosis-frank-ryan |date=2023-02-06 }}. newint.org. Retrieved 5 February 2023.</ref><ref>[https://www.publishersweekly.com/9781603583411 "The Mystery of Metamorphosis: A Scientific Detective Story"]. publishersweekly.com. Retrieved 5 February 2023.</ref><ref>[https://www.washingtonindependentreviewofbooks.com/index.php/bookreview/the-mystery-of-metamorphosis-a-scientific-detective-story/ "The Mystery of Metamorphosis: A Scientific Detective Story"]. washingtonindependentreviewofbooks.com. Retrieved 5 February 2023.</ref><ref>[https://www.washingtonindependentreviewofbooks.com/index.php/features/authors-response-to-independent-review-of-the-mystery-of-metamorphosis "Frank Ryan Responds to the Independent's Review of The Mystery of Metamorphosis"]. washingtonindependentreviewofbooks.com. Retrieved 5 February 2023.</ref>

==Selected publications==

*''The Eskimo Diet: How to Avoid a Heart Attack'' ([[Ebury Press]], 1990)
*''The Eskimo Diet Cookbook'' (Ebury Press, 1990)
*''The Walnut Diet and Fitness Plan'' (Swift, 1993)
*''The Forgotten Plague: How the Battle Against Tuberculosis Was Won - And Lost'' (Back Bay Books, 1994)
*''Virus X: Tracking the New Killer Plagues'' (Back Bay Books, 1997)
*''Darwin's Blind Spot: Evolution Beyond Natural Selection'' ([[Houghton Mifflin]], 2002) 
*''The Brain Food Diet'' (Profile Books, 2007)
*''Metamorphosis: Unmasking the Mystery of How Life Transforms'' ([[Oneworld Publications]], 2011)<ref>Also published as ''The Mystery of Metamorphosis: A Scientific Detective Story'' ([[Chelsea Green Publishing]], 2011)</ref>
*''Virolution: The Most Important Evolutionary Book Since Dawkins' Selfish Gene'' (William Collins, 2013)
*''The Mysterious World of the Human Genome'' ([[Prometheus Books]], 2016)
*''Tuberculosis: The Greatest Story Never Told'' (Swift Publishers, 2019)
